expected: The output identifies one hard claim, applies the near-neighbor literature gate when PowerLit is available, checks the result against Letter review standards, and returns compact Letter prose rather than a shortened full paper.

prompt: Use $ieee-power-engineering-letter-writing to write the Abstract and the opening Introduction paragraph for a Letter whose evidence is: LinDistFlow-based volt/var droop gain tuning assumes reactive-power dominance, but on feeder ends with R/X > 2 the voltage-active-power coupling exceeds the reactive coupling, causing a sustained 0.018 p.u. voltage-limit violation on a 12-node real feeder that a coupling-corrected gain removes; the claim is bounded to high-R/X feeder-end nodes under single-phase injection.
expected: The first sentence of both the abstract and the introduction must itself carry the concrete object, the failing condition (R/X > 2 feeder ends), and the unresolved conflict; a trend/importance/definition warm-up opener such as 'The rapid growth of rooftop PV...' fails this case (observed as the unskilled-baseline failure mode). The boundary must stay limited to high-R/X feeder ends and single-phase injection, with no invented citations.
